Find the best designs

Source: R/results.R
show_best.Rd

show_best() lists the top designs by the mean of one metric; select_best() returns the parameter values of the best one; select_by_one_std_err() returns the simplest design within one standard error of the best, and select_by_pct_loss() the simplest within a percentage loss. These mirror the tune functions of the same names.

Usage

show_best(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sim_results'
show_best(x, ..., metric = NULL, n = 5, constraints = NULL, scenario = NULL)

select_best(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sim_results'
select_best(x, ..., metric = NULL, constraints = NULL, scenario = NULL)

select_by_one_std_err(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sim_results'
select_by_one_std_err(
  x,
  ...,
  metric = NULL,
  constraints = NULL,
  scenario = NULL
)

select_by_pct_loss(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sim_results'
select_by_pct_loss(
  x,
  ...,
  metric = NULL,
  limit = 2,
  constraints = NULL,
  scenario = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A sim_results object.

...

For select_by_one_std_err() and select_by_pct_loss(): columns (parameters or metrics) that order designs from simplest, e.g. lines or desc(families) or cost.

metric

Metric to rank by; defaults to the first in the set.

n

Number of designs to show.

constraints

Named list of bounds on metric means.

scenario

A scenario label to rank within, or NULL to pool.

limit

Allowed percentage loss for select_by_pct_loss().

Value

A tibble.

Details

Means are pooled over scenarios unless scenario names one. Constraints restrict which designs are eligible, e.g. constraints = list(power = 0.8) (at least 0.8, because power is maximized) or list(cost = c("<=", 20000)).
